Should I Hire a Pinterest Manager or Do It Myself?

By Marie Glow StudioUpdated September 23, 2026

Doing Pinterest yourself is a real option, and for plenty of small businesses it is the right one. You know your products better than anyone, you pay no service fees, and you learn how the platform works firsthand. If you have the hours and you enjoy it, that hands-on knowledge is worth having.

So the question behind "should I hire a Pinterest manager" is not whether you are capable. It is whether the weekly work of keyword research, pin design, writing, scheduling and reporting is the best use of your time right now. This page lays the two paths side by side so you can decide with clear eyes.

Hiring a Pinterest manager vs doing it yourself at a glance

Here is how the two paths compare on the factors that matter most. The management column describes Marie Glow Studio's Monthly Pinterest Management.

When doing it yourself is the better pick

Hiring help is not automatically smarter. DIY tends to be the better choice when:

  • You have a few steady hours each week and you like learning platforms. Consistency matters more than perfection on Pinterest, and a small weekly routine beats a burst of activity followed by silence.
  • Your budget is tight and your time is not. DIY costs hours instead of dollars, which is a fair trade early on.
  • You want to understand the platform first. Knowing how Pinterest search works makes you a sharper decision maker later. The Pinterest SEO beginner's guide is a good place to start.
  • You only have a handful of products or pages to promote. A small catalog does not need hundreds of pins a month.
  • You want hands-on control of every pin. Some owners simply prefer to make everything themselves, and that is a valid reason.

If most of that sounds like you, start on your own. If you would like a professional review of what you have built so far, the one-time options are compared in Pinterest audit vs setup vs management.

Why some people choose Marie Glow Studio instead

Owners who hire help are usually not lacking ability. They are lacking hours. Pinterest is a visual search engine, not primarily a social feed, so the work is keywords, titles, descriptions, alt text and steady publishing, and pins keep surfacing for months once they are live. Many owners treat it like Instagram and only pin their own product photos, which tends to get minimal traction. Getting the search side right is a job of its own.

How to decide

Answer these honestly, and count how many you say yes to:

  1. Could I protect several hours every week for Pinterest, for at least three to six months?
  2. Do I enjoy keyword research, design and analytics, or do I dread them?
  3. Would those hours earn me more if I spent them on products, customers or other marketing?
  4. Is the monthly fee something my business can carry comfortably for a few months?
  5. Do I want to learn this skill, or would I rather not have to?

Mostly "yes, I have the time and I want to learn" points to DIY. Mostly "I would rather spend those hours elsewhere" points to a manager.

A realistic word on results

Nobody can guarantee traffic, rankings or sales from Pinterest, whether you do it yourself or hire someone. Results build over weeks and months of consistent effort, which is why three to six months is recommended before judging traction. Our post on how long Pinterest SEO takes explains what to expect. Whichever path you choose, choose the one you can keep up, because steady beats sporadic every time. When you are ready for help, see the Monthly Pinterest Management tiers.

Frequently asked questions

Should I hire a Pinterest manager or do it myself?

Do it yourself if you have steady weekly hours, enjoy learning the platform and have a small catalog. Hire a manager if you would rather spend those hours running the business and want keyword research, pin design, scheduling and reporting handled every month. Neither path guarantees results.

How much does a Pinterest manager cost?
Marie Glow Studio Monthly Pinterest Management starts at $497 per month for 100 pins, $797 per month for 200 pins and $1,097 per month for 300 pins. It is month to month with no minimum, billed in advance.
How long should I give Pinterest management before judging it?

Three to six months is recommended. Pins keep surfacing for months and results build gradually, so a few weeks is usually too short to judge. No one can guarantee traffic, rankings or sales.

Can I start on my own and hire help later?
Yes. Starting DIY, learning the basics and adding professional help when time runs short is a common path. A Pinterest SEO Audit at $197 can review what you have built and give you a ranked 30-day action plan.
Do I have to sign a long contract for Pinterest management?
No. Monthly Pinterest Management is month to month with no minimum commitment and you can cancel anytime. It is billed in advance and non-refundable once work begins for the month.
